theme: News and event databases: GDELT tooling, Google News scrapers, travel-industry news datasets (Skift, PhocusWire), regulatory news trackers

candidates.name: gdeltPyR
candidates.what_it_holds: Python framework that pulls GDELT 1.0 (daily events/GKG back to 1979) and GDELT 2.0 (15-minute events/mentions/GKG) via parallel HTTP GET, returns pandas/geopandas DataFrames or CSV/JSON. No committed dataset itself, just the puller. GPL-3.0, 221 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Could nowcast STR-regulation news flow, travel-shock events, or Airbnb-mention tone (gaps #12 regulation, #14 text/social, #17 methods) at daily/15-min granularity, filterable by CAMEO event codes and country/actor.
candidates.last_activity: unknown exact date; long-running project, 221 commits
candidates.size_hint: acquisition method, not a static file

candidates.name: gdelt-doc-api
candidates.what_it_holds: Lightweight Python client for the GDELT 2.0 DOC API (no BigQuery/S3 needed): article-list DataFrames (URL, title, date, domain, language, source country) and timeline modes (volume, language, source-country, tone) filterable by keyword/domain/country/theme. MIT, 112 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Cheapest way to build a keyword-filtered news-volume/tone timeline for 'Airbnb', 'short-term rental ban', specific city STR ordinances, or travel-industry terms without BigQuery quota; a genuinely lighter-weight alternative to full GDELT for a student team.
candidates.last_activity: unknown exact date; 112 commits, appears active

candidates.name: GoogleNews (Iceloof)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python scraper of Google News search results: title, media source, date, description, link per query; filter by language, region, custom date range. MIT, 135 commits. No bundled data.
candidates.why_useful: Could build a point-in-time news-volume proxy for Airbnb / STR-regulation / travel-demand keyword mentions by date, filterable to specific windows around guide dates -- cheap alternative to paid news APIs. Fragile to Google blocking at scale.
candidates.time_coverage: current + custom date ranges (not a fixed historical archive)

candidates.name: GNews
candidates.what_it_holds: Python package wrapping Google News RSS feeds: title, description, published date, URL, publisher; supports 141+ countries, 41+ languages, optional full-text extraction and Playwright URL resolution. MIT, 235 commits, appears actively maintained.
candidates.why_useful: Same use case as GoogleNews scraper but via RSS (more stable than HTML scraping) -- lower-friction way to track travel-industry / Airbnb / regulation news volume by country and topic.
candidates.last_activity: unknown exact date; 235 commits, actively maintained per repo signals
candidates.time_coverage: current news only (RSS), no historical archive

candidates.name: news-please
candidates.what_it_holds: General-purpose news crawler/extractor (headline, lead, text, image, author, date, language) that can crawl a given news site recursively or via RSS, and specifically supports pulling news articles out of Common Crawl's news archive (CC-NEWS). Apache-2.0, 820 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Could be pointed at Skift, PhocusWire, or other travel-trade press sites (or filtered against CC-NEWS) to build a travel-industry news corpus/timeline; also complements our existing Common Crawl CDX capture (different Common Crawl sub-index, CC-NEWS vs CDX/WARC).
candidates.last_activity: unknown exact date; 820 commits, long-running, widely used research tool
candidates.geography: any site the crawler is pointed at
candidates.time_coverage: CC-NEWS coverage from ~2016-present plus live crawling
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: adjacent to our existing Common Crawl CDX capture over airbnb.com, but this is the CC-NEWS route + generic site crawling, not the same index

candidates.name: event-registry-python (NewsAPI.ai / Event Registry SDK)
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Python SDK for the Event Registry news-event API: article/blog search by keyword, concept, topic, source, sentiment, date; event clustering; trending-concept queries; articles ranked by social shares. MIT, 203 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Event-level (not just article-level) news aggregation could support an events/shocks feed (gap #11) or a regulation-news tracker (gap #12) if Airbnb/STR terms are queried, though free tier is capped at last 30 days and requires an API key.
candidates.time_coverage: free tier: last 30 days only; paid: longer archive

candidates.name: waybackpy
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client/CLI for the Internet Archive Wayback Machine: SavePageNow, CDX Server, and Availability APIs -- retrieve oldest/newest/near-date snapshots of any URL and query custom date ranges. MIT, 497 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Directly the 'Wayback Machine tooling' item in gap #17 -- could retrieve archived Skift/PhocusWire articles, archived airbnb.com pages, or archived AirDNA market pages (gap #2) that are no longer live, without violating current-site ToS.
candidates.last_activity: unknown exact date; 497 commits, actively maintained
candidates.time_coverage: as far back as the Wayback Machine's captures go per URL

candidates.name: newspaper3k / newspaper4k
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library for full-text article and metadata extraction (text, authors, date, images, keywords) from arbitrary news URLs, with parallel multi-threaded downloading; 35+ languages. MIT/Apache-2.0 dual license, 670 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Generic extraction backend that would sit behind a Skift/PhocusWire/regulatory-news crawl once target URLs are identified (e.g. via waybackpy or a sitemap) -- turns raw HTML into structured article records for a text corpus.

candidates.name: pylegiscan
candidates.what_it_holds: Thin Python wrapper around the LegiScan API: search state-legislature bills by state + keyword, pull bill detail and sponsor/legislator info. MIT, 7 commits (small, unmaintained-looking).
candidates.why_useful: Directly matches gap #12's 'Legistar/LegiScan tooling' call-out -- a keyword search for 'short-term rental' across state legislatures could feed a US STR-ordinance/bill tracker; requires a free LegiScan API key.
candidates.last_activity: small repo, 7 commits, no visible recent activity
candidates.time_coverage: current LegiScan bill data (not a static historical file)

candidates.name: openstates-scrapers
candidates.what_it_holds: Open States project's full set of per-state scrapers feeding bills and votes data from every US state legislature into openstates.org; GPL-3.0, 22,236 commits, very large and actively maintained multi-state codebase.
candidates.why_useful: A much larger and more actively maintained alternative to pylegiscan for a US state-level STR-ordinance/bill tracker (gap #12): openstates.org's own bulk data/API (not scraped by us) could be queried for 'short-term rental' bills across all 50 states with full text and status history.
candidates.last_activity: very active, 22,236 commits total on repo
candidates.time_coverage: varies by state, generally multi-year current-session coverage via openstates.org bulk data
candidates.size_hint: large scraper codebase; actual bill data lives on openstates.org, not committed in this repo

candidates.name: Pushshift Reddit API
candidates.what_it_holds: Documentation repo for the (now largely defunct/restricted) Pushshift API for searching Reddit comments/submissions by subreddit, author, date, keyword, with aggregation endpoints; historical archives referenced at files.pushshift.io. No explicit license, 32 commits, examples reference 2017-era usage -- signals the project is stale post-2023 Reddit API changes.
candidates.why_useful: Would be the natural route to r/airbnb, r/AirBnBHosts, r/travel historical dumps (gap #14), but current access is unreliable/restricted since Reddit's 2023 API clampdown -- flag as a lead to verify access, not a working method as of now.
candidates.last_activity: stale; documentation and examples reference 2017, only 32 commits
candidates.time_coverage: historically 2005-2023ish via files.pushshift.io; current access uncertain
candidates.size_hint: pointer to files.pushshift.io archive, size unknown/unverified

notes: Hard constraint hit this run: the session's WebSearch tool returned 'budget exhausted (200 of 200 WebSearch calls)' before I could issue any query for this theme -- that quota is evidently shared across concurrent scout subagents in this sweep, and by the time this scout ran it was already spent. github.com/search HTML pages also 429'd on WebFetch. I fell back to WebFetch-verifying GitHub repos I could recall or infer by exact URL guessing (a materially worse method than search -- likely missed real hits, especially anything Skift/PhocusWire-specific, dedicated Airbnb-GDELT mashups, or STR-ordinance-specific news trackers, none of which I could confirm exist under any URL I could guess). Recommend a re-run of this theme once WebSearch quota resets, focused specifically on: (a) Skift/PhocusWire archive or scrape repos (none found/guessed), (b) GDELT GKG thematic slices already filtered to tourism/travel/regulation themes (V2Themes taxonomy includes TOURISM and could be a committed extract), (c) STR-ordinance-specific news trackers (Airbnb regulation news aggregators) as opposed to generic legislative-bill trackers, (d) Reddit access alternatives post-Pushshift restriction (Arctic Shift, academic Reddit dumps on Zenodo/Academic Torrents). All 11 candidates found are acquisition methods/tooling, not committed datasets -- none fill a gap on their own; each requires nontrivial pull-and-build work plus (for several) a free API key (LegiScan, Event Registry).
